text:
maria: FYI the nightly perf-ci found a regression after last night's kernel autotune sweep on ampere-midseq. seeing ~6% throughput drop for batch=8, seqlen in 512-1024. attaching quick microbench outputs and a short repro run.
perf-ci-bot: nightly-scan completed 2024-11-21 03:12 UTC. job id: nightly-autopick-172345. artifacts: s3://perf-ci/172345/artifacts.tar.gz :spiral_calendar: 
ben: ugh. is this tied to the new batch heuristic change we merged yesterday? 
kai: short read: candidate kernel A (kpick_A_v3) wins latency for small seqlen but seems to degrade for mid-long because it switches to a different tiling path once KV cache threshold exceeded. might be hitting a slower memory layout path.
olivia: @kai can you paste the kbench output?
kai: sure. here is the relevant microbench run (repl):

$ ./kbench --kernel=kpick_A_v3 --arch=ampere --batch=8 --seqlen=768 --kvcache=on --runs=5
run 1 throughput=1038.2 toks/s
run 2 throughput=1025.6 toks/s
run 3 throughput=1032.0 toks/s
avg=1032.6 toks/s

baseline (kpick_stable_v2): avg=1100.3 toks/s
diff = -6.1%

maria: microprobe trace attached in artifact. short excerpt: "tile_select: fallback_to_scalar=true" at iteration ~42.
raj: that fallback smells like an alignment/stride mismatch. we changed the indirect gather kernel in that commit.
ben: who owns that gather kernel?
olivia: @raj and @ben worked on that change in PR #489.
raj: right. quick triage notes: when seqlen>512 and batch>=8 we see the tiling heuristic computing tiles_per_kv = floor(kv_len / tile_sz) which becomes 0 due to integer division when kv_len is slightly smaller than expected (off-by-one from new prefilling). then an assert flips to slower fallback.
maria: so two angles: (1) fix heuristic to avoid zero tiles_per_kv (2) add a targeted autotune override so kpick_A selects the alternative kernel only when tiles_per_kv>1.
kai: i ran a differential run toggling the fix locally: patched heuristic to max(1, floor(...)) and re-ran kbench. results: avg=1096.8 toks/s (~+6% vs broken, -0.3% vs baseline).
ben: nice. patch makes sense but need to add unit + microbench regression test into perf-ci to catch this.
perf-ci-bot: NOTE: nightly-autopick job retained logs. created issue infra#172345 for flaky kernel pick regressions.
maria: can we add a quick repro job in the nightly scan that runs mid-seqlen sweep (seqlen=[512,768,1024], batch=[4,8]) against candidate kernels and requires throughput >= 98% of baseline? if it falls below, fail the candidate gating.
olivia: +1 to gating. where do we keep the baseline numbers?
kai: baselines are in s3://perf-baselines/ampere-midseq/latest.json (artifact includes baseline map). I'll open a PR to wire the check.
raj: deploy plan: patch heuristic in runtime; run a dedicated prober job on perf-lab (8xA100) with the three seqlen points; if green, requeue candidate autotune and trigger a new validation sweep.
ben: estimate 2-3 hours to patch + deploy to staging runtime. after that, I'll kick off the prober run.
maria: prioritizing as P1 for tonight's cycle. @deploy-bot can you schedule a staging deploy window at 06:00 UTC? :alarm_clock: 
deploy-bot: staging deploy scheduled: 2024-11-21 06:00 UTC. window 30m. change-id: cd-172345.
olivia: I'll add a microbench test to kbench-ci that asserts no fallback_to_scalar event in the tile_select trace for mid-seqlen. quick pseudo: 

// test config: ampere, batch=8, seqlen=768
assert(trace.count("fallback_to_scalar") == 0)

maria: thanks. also adding to the rollout checklist: note to update doc 'kernel-pick-behavior.md' to record the tile heuristic and edge cases.
kai: logging note: let's emit a metric kernel.select.fallback with tags {arch, seqlen_bucket, batch} so we can alarm on increases.
raj: logging + perf gate + unit test should close this loop.
ben: after fix landed, re-run nightly candidate sweep tonight and monitor token throughput trends. I'll post an update in this thread once prober finishes.
maria: thanks everyone. cc-ing perf team. summary: cause = off-by-one tiles_per_kv -> scalar fallback; fix = clamp tiles to >=1 + perf-gate in CI; owners: @raj (runtime patch), @kai (autotune PR + gating), @olivia (kbench test), @ben (deploy + prober run).
perf-ci-bot: prober job queued: prober-172345-midseq (target lab: perf-lab-8a100). ETA results ~ 2h.
ben: running now, will update. :eyes:
